title: Checking the debugger settings
description:
Before restarting the VM for kernel debugging, a helper script checks the KDNET settings from lesson 1.02 and prints the command for the host. Write it:

```cpp
struct Kdnet { std::string host; int port{ 0 }; std::string key; };

bool parseSettings(const std::string& text, Kdnet& out, std::string& error);
std::string hostCommand(const Kdnet& k);    // "windbg -k net:port=50005,key=1.2.3.4"
```

The text is `name=value` pairs separated by spaces, in any order: `host=`, `port=` and `key=`, each exactly once. Rules, checked in this order with these errors:

1. a pair without `=`, or an unknown or repeated name: `"bad setting: <the pair>"`
2. any of the three missing: `"missing host"`, `"missing port"` or `"missing key"` (checked in that order)
3. `host` must be an IPv4 address: four numbers 0-255 without leading zeros (`0` itself is fine): `"bad host"`
4. `port` must be a number from 50000 to 50039: `"port must be 50000-50039"`
5. `key` must be four parts separated by dots, each 1 to 13 characters from `0-9` and `a-z` (lower case): `"bad key"`
hints: Write one small `split(text, '.')` helper; both the address and the key are "four parts separated by dots" with different rules per part.
